question: Which South Inida classical dance form literally means 'Story-Play'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The South Indian classical dance form that literally means "story-play" is Kathakali.
 
• The word Kathakali comes from the Malayalam words katha, which means "story" or "conversation", and kaḷi, which means "performance" or "play". 
 
• Kathakali originated in Kerala in the 18th century. 
 
• Kathakali is a combination of dance, drama, music, and ritual.
 
• It's performed with elaborate makeup and costumes, and actors use hand gestures, facial expressions, and eye movements to convey emotions. 
 
• Kathakali performances often depict episodes from the Mahabharata and Ramayana, or the life of Krishna. 
 
• Kathakali is considered one of the most difficult traditional dance forms. 
 
• Other names: Kathakali is also known as the "Saga of East"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Mohiniyattam are all classical Indian dance forms: 
 
• Bharatanatyam
 
• This dance form from Tamil Nadu is based on the ideas of Bharata's Natyashastra.
 
• It's characterized by strong lines, expressive hand gestures, and storytelling through facial expressions. 
 
• Kathak
 
• This dance form from Uttar Pradesh is known for its fluid body movements, complex footwork, fast turns, and sudden stillness
 
• It's still widely practiced in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, and other regions of India. 
 
• Mohiniyattam
 
• This dance form from Kerala is based on the Hindu myth of Vishnu taking the form of Mohini to distract the demon Bhasmasura
